correctness.rationale: The claim is a finite universal statement over exactly 510 nonempty proper vertex subsets. The checker reconstructs the published complex, verifies its 36 facets, face vector and complementarity, proves all 255 face-induced cases are simplices, and replays a validated elementary-collapse certificate for every one of the 255 nonfaces to an exact tetrahedral boundary. Each deletion is checked against the current maximal simplices, so the conclusion is not inferred from homology or from a log.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Broader tightness theory quantifies over every induced subcomplex but only requires injectivity in homology. That does not provide free-face sequences or determine simple-homotopy type, so it does not dominate the new collapse statement.

originality.rationale: Exact-object sources cover complementarity, face/incidence structure, uniqueness, tightness context, and the 36 minimal induced tetrahedral spheres, but no inspected source or semantic search result covers the global elementary-collapse dichotomy for all proper induced subcomplexes. The claim is not a corollary of homology injectivity alone because collapsibility/simple-homotopy is strictly finer than homology.
residual_risks: Arnoux--Marin, DOI 10.2206/kyushumfs.45.167, is a long 1991 crystallographic treatment of the exact complex. Its open-access PDF timed out during retrieval in this run, so only metadata and later descriptions were available; an unindexed equivalent collapse observation there remains possible.
Older unpublished or poorly indexed computational notes could contain the same collapse census. Search failure is not treated as a proof of novelty.

value.rationale: The invariant is motivated by the central role of induced subcomplexes in tight triangulations. The theorem classifies every proper induced subcomplex of the canonical minimal CP2 triangulation into exactly two simple-homotopy types and supplies constructive collapse witnesses. This is a complete structural classification on a canonical object, not an arbitrary finite slice or a routine recomputation of a known face table.
